doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

title: Opening pleasantries and living in New York
summary: Monk Rowe opens the interview, mentions Jane Jarvis and Eddie Locke praising May; May says he was raised in New York and now lives in New Jersey.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are in New York City filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m very pleased to have Earl May with me today. You know you have a lot of people who say nice things about you, did you know that?
Really? No I didn’t know that.
It’s so nice to hear that.
And Eddie Locke and so forth.
So they seem to like your playing as well as you as a person.
That’s doubly nice to hear that.
You’ve been in New York all your life?
All my life. I was born and raised in New York. I’ve been living in New Jersey now for the last twenty-five years or so.
